Python: gap fitting

Source: vignettes/articles/python-gap-fitting.Rmd
python-gap-fitting.Rmd

Filling a dataset’s missing values from its own complete plots: the functions that fit one target or a single model’s targets, their settings, the result and its report, and the neighbour searches the choice is tested with. Filling a dataset’s gaps walks through a fit; a model suite fits its targets through SuitePredictor.predict(gap_fitting=...).

All of the Python reference

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/resolve/r")

# The RESOLVE engine library, downloaded once
library(resolveR)
resolve.install_backend()
pip install resolve-core

fit_gaps() 

fit_gaps(target, raw, recorded, species, coordinates=None, years=None,
         config=GapFittingConfig(), radii=None)

Fits one target’s gaps. target is a GapTarget. raw and recorded are the model’s imputed value and the dataset’s recorded value per plot in the target’s units, (n,) tensors, or (n, 2) latitude and longitude for a geographic target; a NaN recorded value marks a gap. species is the (n, n_species) composition, dense or sparse CSR, an entry other than 0 a species present. coordinates is (n, 2) latitude and longitude (NaN where unknown) and years (n,) survey years; either may be None. radii, a dict of similarity, km and years tensors with one value per complete plot, replaces the drawn hiding distances, so a fit reproduces another implementation’s draw. Returns a GapFit. With no gap the recorded values come back; with fewer than two complete plots the gaps keep the raw imputed value and the report says why.

import numpy as np
import torch
import resolve_core as rc

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
raw = torch.from_numpy(rng.uniform(1950, 2020, 300))
recorded = 1990 + 0.5 * (raw - raw.mean()) + torch.from_numpy(rng.normal(0, 2, 300))
recorded[::5] = float("nan")
species = torch.from_numpy((rng.random((300, 20)) < 0.2).astype("float32"))
fit = rc.fit_gaps(rc.GapTarget("year"), raw, recorded, species)
fit.report["groups"]["unlocated"]["method"]

fit_prediction_gaps() 

fit_prediction_gaps(predictions, species, header=None, columns=None, targets=None,
                    gap_fitting=None)

Fits a single model’s targets from its imputed values (Predictor.predict_dataset) and the dataset’s tables, read in the order of predictions.plot_ids by read_gap_tables. targets maps each target to {"scale": ..., "period": ..., "outputs": [...]}: the scale by name ("linear", "log", "circular", "geographic") and the prediction head(s) read, by default the target’s name; a bearing may read its sine and cosine heads, a location reads its latitude and longitude heads. gap_fitting is a GapFittingConfig, a dict of its fields or None for the defaults. Returns a dict of target to GapFit. fit_prediction_gaps_tables(predictions, tables, requests, config) is the form over a GapTables and a list of GapFitRequest.

read_gap_tables() 

read_gap_tables(species, header=None, columns=None, plot_ids=None)

Reads what gap fitting needs about the plots plot_ids, in that order: the presence of every species the records name, whatever a model’s vocabulary holds, the positions, the survey years and the recorded values. species and header are data frames or CSV paths of the same kind; without header, plot-level columns come from each plot’s first species row. columns is a GapColumns or a dict of plot_id, species_id, latitude, longitude, survey_year and recorded ({target: column}, {target: [latitude, longitude]} for a location). Returns a GapTables. read_gap_tables_csv and read_gap_tables_columns are the forms over CSV paths and string columns.

GapFittingConfig 

GapFittingConfig()
  • candidates (list[GapMethod], default every method): the methods the choice is made among. A method that reads spatial neighbours is a candidate only where the gaps carry coordinates, so the gaps without coordinates need one that reads no position.
  • k_grid (list[int], default [1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50]): the neighbour counts k is chosen from.
  • spatial (bool, default True): spatial neighbours as candidates; False reads composition only.
  • matching_seed (int, default 20261106): the seed of the draw of one gap distance per complete plot and axis.

validate() raises for an empty grid or a k below 1.

GapTarget 

GapTarget(name="", scale=GapScale.Linear, period=360.0)

The target a fit is for: its name (as the report states it), its GapScale and, for a bearing, the length of a full turn in the target’s units.

GapScale

How a target’s values are laid out for fitting: Linear (the value), Log (log1p of the value, for a target whose error is measured on that scale; its local constant is the median), Circular (a bearing as its sine and cosine; a least-squares coefficient is a complex number that turns and shrinks the imputed value) and Geographic (latitude and longitude projected to km of a Lambert azimuthal equal-area plane centred on the complete plots’ geographic median, one coefficient for both axes).

GapMethod

The methods, in the order a tie between equal errors is broken: LocalConstant, Resolve, OffsetSlope, KnnSpecies, StackSpecies, KnnSpatial, StackSpeciesSpatial. Their names in a report and in GapFit.method are local_constant, resolve, offset_slope, knn_species, stack_species, knn_spatial and stack_species_spatial.

GapFit

  • fitted: per plot in the target’s units, shaped as raw: a complete plot’s recorded value, a gap’s fitted value.
  • method (list[str]): "recorded" for a complete plot, the method’s name for a gap; method_codes is the same as an int64 tensor, -1 for a complete plot.
  • report (dict): target, scale, n_complete, n_gaps; axes, per axis (similarity, km, years) whether the test hid by it and the quantiles of the gaps’ distance to their nearest complete plot; neighbours, per kind the k chosen and the error of each k; groups, per group of gaps (located, unlocated) the method chosen, every candidate’s error on the complete plots at the gaps’ distance (matched_error), and for the method chosen its coefficients, n_fitted and k. skipped says why nothing was chosen when that happened.

matched_gap_neighbours() 

matched_gap_neighbours(target, recorded, species, coordinates=None, years=None,
                       config=GapFittingConfig(), radii=None)

The neighbours the choice is tested with, for inspecting a fit: a dict of complete and gaps (the plots’ rows), radii (the distances drawn per complete plot and axis), and species and spatial, each complete plot’s neighbours among the complete plots no nearer to it than its drawn distance ((n_complete, k) indices into complete, -1 after the last; spatial is None without the spatial axis).

GapColumns

The columns read_gap_tables reads: plot_id, species_id, latitude, longitude, survey_year (each str or None) and recorded (list[tuple[str, list[str]]]).

GapTables

What read_gap_tables returns: species (sparse CSR presence, one row per plot), coordinates ((n, 2) or None), years ((n,) or None) and recorded (dict of target to its recorded values, NaN where missing).

GapFitRequest 

GapFitRequest(target, outputs)

One target of a single model for fit_prediction_gaps_tables: its GapTarget and the prediction head(s) it reads.

nearest_by_great_circle() 

nearest_by_great_circle(queries, reference, k, exclude_self=False)

For each row of queries, the k rows of reference nearest to it by great-circle distance, nearest first. Both are (rows, 2) latitude and longitude tensors in degrees. A row with a missing coordinate is never a neighbour and has none. The search is exact and computed in blocks, as nearest_by_cosine is. Returns (indices, km), -1 and NaN where a row has fewer than k.
